 Judgment

01. Appellant-State of Jammu & Kashmir and its functionaries in the Home Department, through the medium of this Miscellaneous Appeal has challenged the Award/Judgment dated November 14,
2009 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu, in File No. 429/Claim titled State Of J&K Through Chief Secretary vs Reeta Sharma on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142270230/
1 - "Reeta Sharma & Ors vs. State of J&K & Ors", whereby for the death of SGC Sat Paul Sharma,
compensation has been awarded to the claimants- respondents in the amount of 18,30,000/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of institution of the petition till realization.
02.

entities.text: Reeta Sharma & Ors vs. State of J&K & Ors"
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
A Gypsy bearing registration No. JK01F-9947, in which the deceased SGC Sat Paul Sharma along with other officials of JKAP were travelling from Jammu to Kashmir Valley on 07.07.2005,
driven by respondent No.5 in a rash and negligent manner when reached near Magar Kote Morh at 7:20 PM met with an accident, as driver lost control over the vehicle resulting into skidding off the vehicle from the road which fell into a deep gorge about 200 feet down causing injuries to SGC Sat Paul Sharma who later on succumbed to the injuries.

In this connection, a case was registered at Police Station Banihal (Ramban) vide FIR No. 111/2005 for commission of offences punishable under sections 279/337/338/304-A RPC and a charge sheet was laid before the Court on conclusion of investigation for the commission of offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338/304-A RPC.
03.

The appellants having been aggrieved of the impugned Award, preferred an above titled appeal,
assailing the award on the grounds that the awarded amount is highly excessive as the Tribunal has wrongly fixed the salary and the likely increase of salary of the deceased; that the Tribunal below has adopted a wrong multiplier as the Claim Tribunal failed to appreciate the facts that the petitioner No.3 i.e respondent No.3 herein was of 65 years of age, moreover, taking into uncertainty of life, the multiplier was liable to be scale down to 11 and the compensation accordingly was to be calculated on the basis of multiplier with the salary actually payable to the deceased after deducting his personal expenses; that the Tribunal has also failed to appreciate the fact that an amount of 10,26,615/- including the Janta Insurance to the tune of 2,50,000/-, special welfare scheme amounting to 6.00 lacs, leave salary of 76,427/- and gratuity of 1,00,188/- had been paid to the respondents, and the Tribunal accordingly has failed to appreciate the aforesaid compensation already paid to the respondents and the aforesaid compensation paid was liable to be deducted or to be taken into account while awarding the awarded amount and it was prayed for setting aside the award.
04.

Pursuant to notice, respondents have filed objections, asserting therein that on account of death of deceased Sat Paul Sharma in Motor Vehicular Accident on 07.07.2005, respondent Nos. 1 to 3 being wife, minor son and mother of the deceased preferred a Claim Petition before the learned Tribunal, which came to be decided on 14.11.2009 and an Award of 18,30,000/- along with 7 %
per annum from the date of institution till liquidation in favour of respondents 1 to 3 to be paid by the respondent-State; that against the said award, the appellant-State preferred an appeal and at the time admission of the appeal, the Court vide order dated 18.05.2012 stayed the execution of the said Award subject to deposit of a sum of 15,00,000/- before the Registry of this Court within a period eight weeks and in the event of deposit of the said amount, an amount of 8,00,000/- was ordered to be released in favour of the claimants; that despite the order of this Court, the appellant-State declined to deposit the awarded amount, but later-on the appellant-State deposited an amount of 15,00,000/- on 13.04.2015.

2 05.

entities.text: State Of J&K Through Chief Secretary vs Reeta Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the impugned award is against the law and the facts, being factually incorrect having been passed in utter disregard to the legal and factual position and is liable to be set aside.
The findings on issue No.1 are both bad and illegal and perverse as the Tribunal failed to record specific findings regarding rash and negligent driving of the vehicle.
It was prayed that the appeal may kindly be allowed and the amount of compensation awarded may kindly be set aside.

06. Learned counsel for the respondents-claimants, ex adverso, argued that the legal heirs of the deceased Sat Paul Sharma filed Claim Petition bearing No. 429/Claim before the Tribunal, wherein on account of death of deceased-Sat Paul Sharma, an amount of 18,30,000/- was awarded as compensation in favour of claimants.

The learned Tribunal while assessing the compensation on the basis of oral evidence as well as the documentary evidence, has rightly taken the basic income of the deceased as 10,000/- and after deducting 1/3rd out of the monthly income of the deceased towards personal expenses and by applying multiplier of 15 has rightly awarded 18,30,000/- in favour of the claimants.

07. Heard learned counsel for both the sides, perused the record and considered the matter.
08.

Respondent Nos. 1 to 3 filed a claim petition in terms of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu seeking compensation for the death of SGC Sat Paul Sharma who had died in a vehicular accident having taken place on 07.07.2005 while travelling by Police Gypsy No. JK01F/9947 from Jammu to Srinagar near Magar Kote on national highway when the driver lost control over the vehicle due to his rash and negligent driving as a result of which vehicle skidded off the road and fell into a deep gorge causing injuries to the deceased - Sat Pal Sharma who later succumbed to those injuries.

09. The Tribunal, after carefully examining the case, decided the claim petition No. 429/Claim on 14.11.2009 in favour of the claimants and granted total compensation of 18,30,000/- including (18,00,000/- for loss of dependency; 15,000/- for funeral expenses and 15,000/- for loss of consortium) along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till liquidation.

10. Aggrieved of the award, the appellants herein challenged the award through the medium of this appeal mainly on the ground that the Tribunal had not slashed down the multiplier due to uncertainties in life and had also failed to appreciate the fact that an amount of 10,26,615/-
including Janta Insurance to the tune of 2,50,000/-, Special Welfare Scheme amounting to 6,00,000/-, Leave Salary 76,427/- and Gratuity of 1,00,188/- had already been paid to the respondents by the appellants herein and the Tribunal had not deducted these amounts while awarding the compensation.

Instead of multiplier of 17 provided in II Schedule of the Act the multiplier was slashed down due to uncertainties of life to 15 having regard to the age of the deceased at 35 years at the time of his death.

11. The first contention of the learned counsel for the appellants that the multiplier should have been scaled down to 11 having regard to the age of 65 years of one of the claimants is not tenable in view State Of J&K Through Chief Secretary vs Reeta Sharma on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142270230/
3 of the fact that the multiplier has to be applied having regard to the age of the deceased and not the claimant and in my considered opinion the applied multiplier of 15 was properly used by the Tribunal for computation of the compensation.
12.

entities.text: State Of J&K Through Chief Secretary vs Reeta Sharma
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as the second contention that the amount granted under Janta Insurance Special Welfare Scheme, Leave Salary & Gratuity should have been deducted or adjusted while computing the compensation is also misplaced in view of the fact that these amounts are otherwise ought to be granted to the legal heirs of a policeman who may have died even in a natural death irrespective of the death, in accident.

13. So far as the contention raised by the appellant-State that the learned Tribunal has not taken note of the amount paid to the respondents towards Janata Insurance, Special Welfare Scheme,
gratuity as well as leave salary is concerned, the Supreme Court in case titled - "Helen C. Rebello Vs.
Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation" reported in 1999 ACJ 10 (SC) has held that provident fund, pension, insurance and similarly any cash, bank balance, shares, fixed deposits, etc.
are all a 'pecuniary advantage' receivable by the heirs on account of one's death have no co-relation with the amount of compensation on account of accidental death.

entities.text:
Helen C. Rebello Vs.
Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation" reported in 1999 ACJ 10 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Therefore, the amounts granted under these heads to the family of the deceased-policeman are not deductable to calculate the compensation.

I find support to hold this view in view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case titled "Helen C. Rebello" (supra) wherein it had been held that provident fund, pension, insurance and similarly any cash, bank balance, shares, fixed deposits, etc.
are all a pecuniary advantage receivable by the heirs on account of once death have no co-relation with the amount of compensation on account of accidental death.
15.
Viewed thus, the appeal is found to be devoid of any merit and substance and is liable to be rejected.
The appeal is, thus, dismissed and the impugned award is upheld.

16. The awarded amount, if any, deposited with the Registry of this Court and not released earlier in favour of the claimants, shall be released in their favour in terms of the award passed by the Tribunal after proper identification of the claimants and after charging the Court fees under rules.
17. The Appeal is thus disposed of as dismissed.
Tribunal record be sent down forthwith alongwith a copy of this judgment for information and record.
(M A CHOWDHARY) JUDGE JAMMU 13 .09.2024
